name: StrongMinds (Founders Pledge, 2018)
beneficiaries_note: The countries the model's summary names, sharing equally: Uganda, Zambia.
summary: Group interpersonal therapy for depression, mostly for women, in Uganda and Zambia. A re-implementation of Founders Pledge's 2018 cost-effectiveness analysis, which turns StrongMinds' reported, uncontrolled fall in depression scores into DALYs averted by spreading the disability weight of severe depression over the 27-point scale. That route, not the evidence alone, is why it comes out far below HLI's wellbeing-based model of the same charity.

source.title: Women's Empowerment cause report (2018) and Mental Health cause report (2019): StrongMinds cost-effectiveness analysis

sections.title: Discounting
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Founders Pledge's. Founders Pledge counts a year of less depression the same whenever it comes. In our view later years count less at the discount rate under Your values; Founders Pledge's view sets the rate to 0, so its numbers reproduce.

sections.title: Our steps: per dollar, and staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' steps after Founders Pledge's bottom line: the cost per outcome turned into outcomes per dollar, then credit by share of resources (staff's forgone pay), which is off by default and in Founders Pledge's view.

rows.label: Average reduction in PHQ-9 score per participant, as first reported

source.title: Founders Pledge, Women's Empowerment cost-effectiveness analyses (2018)

rows.explainer: StrongMinds' own end-of-treatment result: the average fall in depression score (PHQ-9, 0–27) among participants, from its 2015 Phase 2 evaluation, as Founders Pledge took it. It is a before-and-after change with no control group, so it includes people who would have recovered anyway; Founders Pledge's adjustment below doesn't remove that. No range published.

rows.label: Adjustment to the average reduction in PHQ-9 score

source.title: Founders Pledge, Women's Empowerment cost-effectiveness analyses (2018)
source.note: Sheet formula =(10/95)*13; StrongMinds 'Follow Up Evaluations for Phase 1 & Phase 2' (2017)

rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's deduction from the reported fall, written in the sheet as (10/95) × 13 and based on StrongMinds' 2017 follow-up evaluations. The sheet doesn't spell out the reasoning; we keep its number.

Minimum PHQ-9 score

source.title: Founders Pledge, Women's Empowerment cost-effectiveness analyses (2018)

rows.explainer: The lowest possible score on the PHQ-9 depression questionnaire. Shown as in the sheet; nothing uses it.

rows.label: Maximum PHQ-9 score

source.title: Founders Pledge, Women's Empowerment cost-effectiveness analyses (2018)

rows.explainer: The highest possible score on the PHQ-9 depression questionnaire (nine questions scored 0–3).

rows.label: DALY weighting of severe major depressive disorder

source.title: Founders Pledge, Women's Empowerment cost-effectiveness analyses (2018)

rows.explainer: The Global Burden of Disease disability weight for severe major depression, 0.658 (GBD 2016, which Founders Pledge used, and GBD 2019 agree; shared fact).

rows.label: DALY weighting per point on the PHQ-9 scale (healthy years per point-year)
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency. Founders Pledge spreads the weight of severe depression evenly over the 27 points of the scale (0.658 / 27 = 0.0244 per point, StrongMinds!C9). The site counts every fall in depression on the PHQ-9 the same way, for every model: 0.031 healthy years per point for a year, the Global Burden of Disease weights for mild, moderate and severe depression placed on the PHQ-9's severity bands (shared fact). That counts a fall from severe to mild as GBD does, where Founders Pledge's even spread gives less per point. The evaluator view uses Founders Pledge's 0.0244.

rows.label: DALYs averted per year per participant directly after treatment
Retention rate of benefits (share kept each year)

source.title: Founders Pledge, Women's Empowerment cost-effectiveness analyses (2018)
source.note: Reay et al. (2012); StrongMinds 'Follow Up Evaluations for Phase 1 & Phase 2' (2017)

rows.explainer: The share of the benefit left a year later. Founders Pledge's conservative case halves it in two years (1/√2), the optimistic in three (1/2^(1/3)); the best guess is the median of the two (cell C11 is =MEDIAN(B11,D11)). Range from the sheet.

rows.label: Total DALYs averted per participant
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's sum over all years of a benefit that keeps the retention rate each year, each year counted at the average of its start and end. Times our discount factor, which is 1 in Founders Pledge's view.

rows.label: Cost per beneficiary (USD)

source.title: Founders Pledge, Women's Empowerment cost-effectiveness analyses (2018)

rows.explainer: StrongMinds' cost per person treated in 2018, from its Q2 2018 report, as Founders Pledge took it.

rows.label: Cost per DALY averted (USD)
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's bottom line: $377 per DALY averted ($304–454 across its conservative and optimistic retention).

rows.label: Cost per year of severe major depressive disorder prevented (USD)
rows.explainer: The same result per year of severe depression averted, the figure Founders Pledge's 2019 mental health report quotes ($248).

rows.label: Discount rate on future benefits
rows.explainer: The shared discount rate (Your values). Founders Pledge doesn't discount these benefits, so its view pins the rate at 0.

rows.label: Discount factor on benefits that fade year by year
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge counts a benefit that keeps a fixed share of itself each year (the retention rate), summed over all years, without discounting. Discounting each year's benefit at the shared rate turns the sum 1 / (1 − r) into 1 / (1 − r / (1 + rate)); this is the ratio of the two. At a rate of 0 it is 1, so Founders Pledge's figures reproduce.

rows.label: Household size of psychotherapy recipients
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** Every model reads one household size per place: the latest DHS figure for Uganda (`@household_size.uganda`, 4.7). Founders Pledge's sheet counts no household.

rows.label: Household spillover of psychotherapy, as a share of the recipient's own effect
rows.explainer: The shared spillover ratio (facts: wellby_factors.household_spillover_ratio_psychotherapy), as in HLI's and SoGive's StrongMinds models.

rows.label: Household multiplier: everyone who benefits, per participant
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: HLI and SoGive count the benefit therapy brings the rest of the household, each other member gaining about 16% of the participant's own; Founders Pledge counts the participant only (1 in the evaluator view). Our view counts the household in every psychotherapy model, from the shared figures, so the three StrongMinds analyses differ only in what they measured.

rows.label: DALYs averted per dollar, household included
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's cost per DALY turned around.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for programs where staff deliver the help themselves (treatment, counselling, coaching, outreach): staff pay is about half the cost. Our judgment; we haven't seen this program's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Health workers and field staff at nonprofits often earn somewhat less than in comparable jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: DALYs averted per donor dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
